Bit-level substrate of the arithmetic half of the coding repair: least-significant-bit extraction and halving (parity/half/twice), the bundling code codeBits with its extraction lemma pair, the round-trip on a bit list whose length is supplied, and the bound that the code dominates its own length (so a future parser can take its fuel from the code itself). The symbol layer (self-delimiting var/num index bits and constructor tags), the parser with its default branch and the round-trip on the image remain open.

Closes the coding-repair obligation of CodingRepair (C-163/C-164/C-165) at the coding layer: the self-delimiting unary index layer, the symbol layer (two tag bits for var/num plus their index, one tag bit for application) with a streaming parser whose round trip is fuel-exact (a frame stack solves sequential consumption while terminating structurally on the fuel), the length/bound/extra-fuel bookkeeping, and finally the repaired coder codeT' = codeBits . bits with a total decoder dec (default branches included) and round trip dec (codeT' t) = t, hence injectivity by C-164. Only Tm coding/decoding is covered: the proof predicate P, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open and ERCF-3 stays gated.

Lifts the repaired coding from Tm (C-176) to Fml, which is the layer the diagonal machinery actually quotes. The formula symbol layer (two tag bits for =f/bot/=>f, plus the binder index of all) comes with a streaming parser whose round trip is exact in the iteration count; the Tm children of =f are handed to the term-level parser as a black box (fuel = the length of the remaining bit list); the length bound STEPS <= LEN makes the repaired formula code its own fuel; and codeF' = codeBits . bitsF comes with a total decoder decF and the round trip decF (codeF' phi) = phi, hence injectivity. Only Fml coding/decoding is covered: formula-layer substitution alignment, proof-predicate representability, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open, and ERCF-3 stays gated.

Substitution and quotation over the repaired coding. With a decoder in hand, code-level substitution can be defined as decode-substitute-encode, and the agreement with syntax-level substitution becomes a corollary: substCodeT k n (codeT' t) = codeT' (substT k n t) and substCodeF k n (codeF' phi) = codeF' (substF k n phi). Quotation (the numeral of the repaired formula code) is injective, and the diagonal instance is a substitution instance of the same formula whose code is reached by the code-level substitution. Honest boundary: these code-level functions are defined through the decoder, so nothing here claims that the object theory can represent them -- representability, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open and ERCF-3 stays gated.
